priceSnapshot.note: REPUBLISHED AT THE PROPER SLOT. This file replaces a version of the same report written at 23:32 COT last night, two and a half hours early, because the scheduler stacked 30 August's morning, endday and this midnight session into a twenty-five-minute burst. That early version had a seven-minute comparison window and admitted it. This one is the 02:07 COT read the midnight slot is for, and the tape has done real work in between: spot is 78,045.3 against the 77,510.0 that early version printed, up 535.3 points or 0.69 percent, after a V-shaped reversal that put in the 24h low at 77,000.0 and then squeezed shorts back through 78,000. Only ONE ledger run is permitted per session and the 23:32 run already made it, so the paper wallet is NOT re-traded here - see the Paper wallet section. Everything else in this file is recomputed from live feeds.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 77,400.0 and no reclaim on either of the next two hourly bars. INHERITED UNCHANGED for a fourth consecutive report - and this is the first one where the gate was actually TESTED rather than merely watched. Price traded to 77,000.0 at 04:45Z, a full 400 points beneath the level, yet the lowest 1H CLOSE of the entire move was 77,473.7 at 06:00Z. The gate was pierced on the wick and never confirmed on a close. That is precisely the outcome the two-bar confirmation rule exists to produce, and it is the strongest evidence this log has yet gathered that the rule earns its keep.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 78,300.0. RAISED from the 78,180.0 the last three reports carried, and the reason is that 78,180.0 has now been consumed: the 05:00Z bar printed a 78,183.4 high, touched the level and closed 77,940.5 without confirming. A gate that has been tagged and rejected is no longer information. 78,300.0 is the level that matters next because it clears the 1H EMA50 at 78,253.5, the 4H EMA20 at 78,270.4 and the 1H EMA100 at 78,296.0 in a single move - three separate overhead references inside 43 points. Reclaim that band on a close and the intraday downtrend is finished; this is the trigger the MORNING session should be watching.

decisionBox.changed: ONE GATE MOVES, and it moves because it was hit. The add trigger goes from 78,180.0 to 78,300.0 after the 05:00Z bar tagged 78,183.4 and failed to close above it. The reduce gate stays at 77,400.0, now materially stronger than it was: it survived a 400-point wick to 77,000.0 without a single hourly close beneath it. FOUR things are genuinely new since the 23:32 file. FIRST, the 77,000.0 defence - a round number, the 24h low, and the level where forced long selling was concentrated - held and produced a V reversal. SECOND, the liquidation tape has FLIPPED SIDES. The 23:32 run measured 204,729 USD of forced long selling against 2,981 USD of short covering, 68.7 to one bearish. The window since then measures 859,724 USD of SHORT liquidations against 134,759 USD of long, 6.4 to one the other way. Shorts positioned for continuation below 77,400 got run over between 77,900 and 78,130. THIRD, the bounce is spot-led, not leverage-led: funding is 0.0000792474500719 per 8h - positive, longs pay, but only 0.0079 percent - and the premium is NEGATIVE at -0.0004407589253682, so the perpetual is still trading UNDER the index even after a 1,045-point rally off the low. Open interest is 2,138,951,108.62 USD, up only 1.54 percent from the 2,106,444,470.75 the early file recorded, and the retail long/short account ratio is 1.15 against 1.14 - positioning has barely rebuilt. A rally that shorts are paying for and longs have not crowded into is the healthy kind. FOURTH, and cutting against all of it, Brent is 90.52, up 2.75 percent on the session after US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers preparing to mine the Strait of Hormuz. That is a fresh inflation shock landing into a market that already repriced September after Warsh, US10Y is 4.718, and US equity futures are red with US100 at 29,353 down 0.27 percent. BTC rallying into an oil shock is the anomaly in tonight's tape and it is the single reason the bias is range-with-a-tilt rather than bullish. The stop stays RECOMMENDED at 76,850.0, just beneath the 76,888.0 invalidation: the next report is the 06:50 morning session and it spans the European open.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is UP and the flip is the headline. Short-side forced buying totals 859,724 USD against 134,759 USD of long-side forced selling, 6.38 to one, an almost exact mirror of the 68.7-to-one bearish reading the 23:32 file measured two and a half hours earlier. The whole long-side band sits between 77,350 and 77,600 and price has already traded through it, wicked to 77,000 and reclaimed everything. Two honest caveats. These are REALIZED fills, so they mark where fuel was spent rather than where it rests - the OKX free feed gives no forward heatmap. And the short-side cluster thins to 406 USD at 78,150, which says the squeeze exhausted its supply of stops 33 points below the session high rather than being turned back by sellers. That is a bounce that ran out of buyers, not one that met a wall, and it is why the range case still carries the most probability.

divergences.note: Confirmed and already resolved. The 23:30 COT bar closed 77,479.3 with RSI(14) at 21.7, deeply oversold. The 01:00 COT bar closed 77,473.7 - 5.6 points LOWER - with RSI at 35.2, a 13.5-point higher momentum low. Price made a marginal lower low, momentum made a decisive higher one, and the resolution followed inside the hour with the squeeze through 78,000. This is the cleanest divergence this log has recorded in the current sequence and it is the mechanical reason the 15m MACD histogram is the only positive one on the board. SCHEMA NOTE for future runs: the app's DivergenceSchema requires type in regular_bullish|regular_bearish|hidden_bullish|hidden_bearish, oscillator in rsi|macd lowercase, and priceFrom/priceTo as {t, price} OBJECTS - not the bare numbers the desk skill's shorthand implies. The field carries .catch([]) so a malformed entry is silently dropped rather than blanking the report, which is exactly how this would go unnoticed.

calibration.rollingRecord: Twenty-two sessions logged. The 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band tally gains its most instructive entry yet and now reads: four clean confirmations, two whipsaws, one gate that whipsawed then confirmed on the second trigger, one that triggered twice and was voided both times, one report - 30 August midnight - whose ADD and REDUCE gates both fired in that order nine hours apart, and now one window in which BOTH standing gates were pierced intraday and NEITHER confirmed on a close.
calibration.note: THE RESULT WORTH KEEPING FROM THIS RUN. Between 04:30Z and 06:00Z the 77,400.0 reduce gate was pierced by 400 points, to 77,000.0, and the 78,180.0 add gate was tagged at 78,183.4. Neither confirmed. The lowest settled 1H close of the entire move was 77,473.7, 73.7 points ABOVE the reduce level, and the highest settled 1H close was 78,080.0, a hundred points BELOW the add level. A desk trading the raw levels would have sold the low and bought the high inside ninety minutes. The two-bar close-confirmation rule caught both and produced no trade, which is the correct outcome and the first time this log has been able to demonstrate that with a same-window double test. priorReduceFired is FALSE in the strong sense now - tested and held, not merely untouched. actingHelped is null because no action was taken to grade. PROCESS NOTE, carried forward and now partly acted on: the 23:32 run flagged that three reports written inside twenty-five minutes would leave near-duplicate calibration rows and silently triple-count one market state.
